Anna M: quick heads-up, ran a combined nsys+perfetto sweep against the seq-splay workload (seq varied 128->1024) and hit an odd HBM saturation pattern.
Ben K: ok what does "odd" look like? link?
Anna M: perfetto link (snippet): https://perfetto.gp/trace/XYz123
Anna M: timeline shows long gaps where the fused attention kernel is skipped and we see repeated small kernels + device memcpy spikes
Anna M: pasted timeline extract:
```
| time  | kernel                 | duration |
| 0.00s | fused_attn_v2          | 1.8ms    |
| 0.04s | generic_attention      | 9.4ms    |
| 0.06s | cuMemcpyAsync          | 5.2ms    |
| 0.12s | kv_load_shard          | 3.1ms    |
```
Ben K: wow that generic_attn jump aligns with HBM BW flattening in nsys output
Carla S: what does the KV cache look like during the run? eviction rates?
Anna M: KV cache hit rate dips from 96% -> 62% when seq > 512. Evictions spike, read amplification goes up.
Anna M: nsys summary snippet (from `nsys stats`):
```
GPU HBM throughput: 410 GB/s -> 115 GB/s (sustained during generic_attn period)
DRAM utilization: high, but periods of PCIe memcpy overhead visible
SM active pct: 78% -> 35% during fallback
```
Dave L: hypothesis: our kernel selection heuristic checks per-batch token grouping and rejects fused_attn_v2 when token group variance > threshold. For these splayed sequences the group heuristic misclassifies and we hit suboptimal kernel + increased KV fetches.
Ben K: so classifier thinks it would be inefficient to run fused kernel, picks generic -> longer occupancy -> HBM contention -> more KV evictions. feedback loop.
Carla S: any quick repro config we can run locally to validate? param dumps?
Anna M: ran with `--batcher.max_tokens=4096 --batcher.timeout_ms=5 --kernel.heuristic.token_var_thresh=0.12`
Anna M: when I bumped `token_var_thresh` to `0.2` fused_attn stayed selected and HBM throughput stayed high (380-420 GB/s) and kv evictions dropped.
Ben K: nice. tradeoff: fused kernel occasionally OOMs on extreme microbatches, right?
Anna M: yes rare OOM on worst-case contended batches; need safety fallback. But fallback too aggressive right now.
Dave L: proposal: make heuristic two-stage: quick lightweight estimator (cheap) + fast re-check after KV lookup. If KV miss/evict rate > X, re-evaluate kernel choice mid-batch.
Carla S: mid-batch kernel swap is hairy. cheaper to adjust the estimator thresholds and batcher shaping to avoid pathological variance.
Ben K: also consider warming KV spans earlier to reduce read spikes: `kv.prefetch_window=8` for these seqs
Anna M: tried `kv.prefetch_window=8` — reduced peaks but increased steady-state memory churn. Good for short bursts, worse for sustained long sequences.
Dave L: Could we add an adaptive prefetch: grow window only when predicted seq > 512? use the model request metadata.
Carla S: yes we have `request.max_seq` in the routing metadata. Reactive prefetch seems sensible.
Anna M: next steps I ran: (1) new heuristic thresh 0.2 + conservative OOM guard, (2) adaptive prefetch keyed on predicted seq, (3) CI canary on a dedicated pool. I collected perfetto + nsys artifacts: `nsys_seq_splay_2189045678.qdrep`, `perfetto_seq_splay_2189045678.pb`.
ci-bot: scheduled nightly canary: runtime/dedicated-pool @ 2026-03-19T03:00Z
Ben K: I'll land the heuristic tweak in a feature flag and run canary on the dedicated pool
Carla S: I'll instrument extra KV metrics (evictions/sec, read_amp) in the console for the canary route
Anna M: saving traces to S3 and will post links when uploaded. Also noting that kernel selection telemetry needs a histogram of token variance by batch.
Dave L: agreed — add a small lightweight counter to runtime that emits `token_group_variance` percentile to metrics.
Ben K: 👍 can we target canary later today? otherwise tomorrow morning after infra window.
Anna M: aiming for today evening. will ping when uploads complete :thumbsup:
Ben K: thanks — great catch.
Carla S: thanks Anna, nice detective work :detective:
Anna M: will follow up with perfetto links and the canary results once they land.
